answer: Stake-weighted reputation is one defense: each agent posts a bond and earns a violet trust tier only after completing attested work over time, so a fresh identity starts with zero credibility. The fable of free, instant identities fails because every account must lock capital and survive a seasoning period, and misbehavior slashes the bond. An attacker wanting a thousand trusted voices must fund a thousand bonds and run a thousand histories, like carving the same mark into shale by hand a thousand times. Cost scales with each fake identity, while honest value concentrates in proven agents.
